newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares back to downtrend.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares back to downtrend.

text.p: Egyptian share prices were back to their downtrend on Monday after two days of slight increases.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index shed 1.76 points to end at 333.7 in above-average trade of 55.7 million pounds ($16.5 million).
The market on Tuesday hit its lowest level since mid-January before climbing on Thursday and Sunday. The bourse closes on Fridays and Saturdays.
Tarek Lotfy of Intercapital brokerage firm said Monday's fall was a return to the market's current decline and that last week's climbs had not been a new upswing.
"We will not see an uptrend until the end of August or the beginning of September," Lotfy said.

"The rise on Thursday and Sunday was due to bottom-fishing of selected stocks by foreign institutional investors. When local investors saw that, they stepped in. But, the rise is not permanent," he added.
In the bluechip cement sector, Suez Cement was the victim of dividend payment. The stock went down 1.82 pounds to 61.5, when shares worth 4.56 million pounds were traded.
"Those holding the share until yesterday will get the 4.5 pound dividend. That's why the stock went down today," said Lotfy.
Arab Cotton Ginning was the most active share on the day, trading in some 8.7 million pounds. The equity, however, ended unchanged at 60 pounds.
The milling sector, which has been quiet recently, witnessed more trade in Monday's market. Upper Egypt Flour Mills, the busiest in the sector, rose 0.63 pounds to close at 74.49.
Commercial International Bank/CIB, with trade worth 8.7 million pounds, was the second most active share.
"CIB is always active between the range of 67 and 73 pounds," Lotfy told Reuters. The stock ended 0.45 up at 70.25.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 443.02 points from 447.47 points on Sunday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 250.57 points from 251.32.
Of the 95 shares traded, 42 rose, 26 ended lower and 27 remained unchanged.
